newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Ruling on Zambia's Konkola North within five years.
newsitem.headline: Ruling on Zambia's Konkola North within five years.

text.p: A decision on the development of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines' (ZCCM) Konkola North mine can be made within the next five years, the Zambian Finance Ministry said on Friday.
South African mining house Anglovaal Ltd is expected to sign an agreement on the development of Konkola North by February, the Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said earlier on Friday.
"An option agreement between Anglovaal and Zambia is expected to be signed within two months," ZPA chief Valentine Chitalu told Reuters.
The agreement would see Anglovaal agreeing to conduct a feasibility study on the project over the next two year and develop the mine if the study proved conclusive.
The finance ministry said in a statement that Anglovaal's minerals division Avmin had won the option to acquire a majority interest in Konkola North.
"The option will be exercisable once the bankable feasibility study is completed.

"It is envisaged that a development decision on Konkola North could be made within five years, provided that the results of the work performed by Avmin confirm the economic feasibility of a substantial new mine," the ministry said.

It added that Anglovaal had agreed to introduce another major international mining house as a partner in the development of Konkola North and also to procure or provide 100 percent of the financing of the mine development if a decision was taken to develop Konkola North.

Development of the Konkola ore body, which also includes the separate Konkola Deep mine, is seen as crucial to the future of Zambia's copper industry, since reserves at ZCCM's main Nchanga pit will run out by the end of the century.
Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd is leading a consortium seeking to develop the Konkola Deep mine.
